sources.title: Statistical Consequences of Fat Tails
sources.claim: Under fat-tailed distributions, conventional estimators, Gaussian asymptotics, variance-based risk measures and finite-sample intuition can become unreliable; model uncertainty compounds the problem.

sources.title: On the Statistical Differences between Binary Forecasts and Real World Payoffs
sources.claim: Binary forecast accuracy and real-world payoff performance are not equivalent, especially under nonlinear payoffs and fat-tailed distributions.

sources.title: Tail Risk Constraints and Maximum Entropy
sources.authors: Donald Geman; Helyette Geman; Nassim Nicholas Taleb
sources.claim: Portfolio design under uncertainty can be dominated by explicit left-tail constraints, with barbell-like allocations emerging when distributions are only partially known.

sources.title: The Variation of Certain Speculative Prices
sources.claim: Speculative price changes can exhibit heavy tails that are poorly represented by Gaussian assumptions.

sources.title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
sources.claim: People evaluate risky choices relative to reference points and display asymmetric responses to gains and losses, including loss aversion.

sources.title: Does the Stock Market Overreact?
sources.authors: Werner F. M. De Bondt; Richard Thaler
sources.claim: Long-horizon stock return evidence is consistent with investor overreaction, with prior losers subsequently outperforming prior winners in the studied sample.

sources.title: Investor Sentiment and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
sources.claim: Investor sentiment has stronger subsequent return effects among securities that are difficult to value and difficult to arbitrage.

sources.title: A Model of Investor Sentiment
sources.authors: Nicholas Barberis; Andrei Shleifer; Robert W. Vishny
sources.claim: A parsimonious belief-updating model can generate both underreaction to news and overreaction to a sequence of similar news.

sources.title: A Unified Theory of Underreaction, Momentum Trading, and Overreaction in Asset Markets
sources.claim: Gradual information diffusion can produce short-run underreaction and momentum, while trend chasing can contribute to longer-run overreaction.

sources.title: The Limits of Arbitrage
sources.claim: Capital constraints and delegated professional arbitrage can allow mispricing to persist or widen, especially in extreme conditions.

sources.title: Liquidity Risk and Expected Stock Returns
sources.claim: Exposure to aggregate liquidity fluctuations is priced in the cross-section of expected stock returns.

sources.title: Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading
sources.claim: Market depth and price impact emerge endogenously as informed trading is absorbed by competitive market makers in the presence of noise trading.

sources.title: Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity with Estimates of the Variance of United Kingdom Inflation
sources.claim: Conditional variance can change predictably over time, motivating explicit modelling of volatility clustering.

sources.title: Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity
sources.claim: GARCH models capture persistent conditional volatility with a parsimonious autoregressive structure.

sources.title: Common risk factors in the returns on stocks and bonds
sources.authors: Eugene F. Fama; Kenneth R. French
sources.claim: Multiple common factors beyond the market factor help explain average stock and bond returns.

sources.title: A five-factor asset pricing model
sources.authors: Eugene F. Fama; Kenneth R. French
sources.claim: Profitability and investment factors add explanatory power to the traditional market, size and value factors.

sources.title: Kenneth R. French Data Library
sources.claim: The library provides maintained research factor returns and portfolio data used widely for empirical asset-pricing validation.

sources.title: Betting Against Beta
sources.claim: Leverage constraints can lead investors to overweight high-beta assets, creating a low-beta versus high-beta return spread across markets.

sources.title: Quality Minus Junk
sources.authors: Cliff Asness; Andrea Frazzini; Lasse H. Pedersen
sources.claim: A broad quality characteristic built from profitability, growth and safety has historically been associated with strong risk-adjusted returns across markets.

sources.title: Understanding Style Premia
sources.claim: Value, momentum, carry and defensive styles have long-run evidence across asset classes and can diversify each other when implemented systematically.

sources.title: Fact, Fiction and Momentum Investing
sources.authors: Cliff Asness; Andrea Frazzini; Ronen Israel; Tobias J. Moskowitz
sources.claim: Momentum evidence is broad across long histories, countries and asset classes, though implementation and diversification matter.

sources.title: Demystifying Managed Futures
sources.authors: Brian K. Hurst; Yao Hua Ooi; Lasse H. Pedersen
sources.claim: Simple time-series momentum strategies explain a substantial portion of managed-futures behaviour across commodities, rates, equities and currencies.

sources.title: Trend Following: Equity and Bond Crisis Alpha
sources.claim: Long-run trend-following evidence shows positive skew and crisis-alpha characteristics across equity and bond stress environments.

sources.title: A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
sources.claim: A simple trend-based tactical allocation framework can materially alter drawdowns and risk-adjusted outcomes across asset classes in historical tests.

sources.title: A Quantitative Approach to Faber's Tactical Asset Allocation
sources.authors: Stefano Marmi; Claudio Pacati; Wiston Adrian Risso; Roberto Reno
sources.claim: Trading-rule evidence requires bootstrap and robustness analysis before being interpreted as a violation of market efficiency or a persistent edge.

sources.title: Fundamental Indexation
sources.authors: Robert D. Arnott; Jason C. Hsu; Philip Moore
sources.claim: Non-capitalization-weighted fundamental index constructions can exhibit different risk-return characteristics from cap-weighted benchmarks.

sources.title: Overconfident Investors, Predictable Returns, and Excessive Trading
sources.claim: Investor overconfidence can contribute to excessive trading, high volume and predictable return patterns.

sources.title: Investor Psychology and Security Market Under- and Overreactions
sources.authors: Kent Daniel; David Hirshleifer; Avanidhar Subrahmanyam
sources.claim: Overconfidence and biased self-attribution can generate short-run momentum and longer-run reversals.

sources.title: Commonality in liquidity
sources.authors: Tarun Chordia; Richard Roll; Avanidhar Subrahmanyam
sources.claim: Liquidity has an important market-wide common component, so execution conditions can deteriorate jointly across securities.

sources.title: Margin-Based Asset Pricing and Deviations from the Law of One Price
sources.claim: Margin requirements and funding constraints can create persistent relative-value deviations and amplify losses during funding stress.

sources.title: Liquidity and leverage
sources.claim: Financial intermediaries' balance-sheet leverage is procyclical and can amplify liquidity conditions and asset-price movements.

sources.title: Noise
sources.claim: Noise trading and imperfect information are integral to market functioning, making observed price changes a mixture of information and noise.

sources.title: On the Impossibility of Informationally Efficient Markets
sources.authors: Sanford J. Grossman; Joseph E. Stiglitz
sources.claim: Perfect informational efficiency is incompatible with costly information acquisition because prices must leave some reward for informed analysis.

sources.title: Richard Donchian Trend Following Rules
sources.claim: The public Donchian rule compilation emphasizes following clearly defined moves, limiting losses, riding profits and reducing commitments when the market state is uncertain.

rules.hypothesis: Extremely high realized volatility indicates a state where Gaussian-style confidence and ordinary sizing are unreliable.
rules.mechanism: Fat tails and finite-sample instability make variance-based confidence fragile in extremes.
rules.formalization_note: VERITAS proxy. The 9% threshold is provisional and must be validated.

rules.hypothesis: Rule promotion must not optimize hit rate alone; payoff magnitude, asymmetry, MFE, MAE and tail losses must be evaluated separately.
rules.mechanism: Binary forecast skill and continuous payoff performance are different objects.

rules.hypothesis: When distributional uncertainty is large, portfolio construction should explicitly constrain left-tail exposure rather than rely on point-estimated mean-variance optimization.
rules.mechanism: Tail constraints dominate under partial distributional knowledge.
rules.formalization_note: Governance only until portfolio engine is implemented.

rules.hypothesis: Extreme volatility with abnormal activity may indicate a heavy-tail regime in which extrapolating ordinary return distributions is unsafe.
rules.mechanism: Speculative-price distributions can have much heavier tails than Gaussian models imply.

rules.hypothesis: Decision review must detect reference-point anchoring, loss aversion and asymmetric treatment of gains versus losses.
rules.mechanism: Human choices under risk depend on reference points and asymmetric value functions.
rules.formalization_note: Governance for human/LLM review; not a market timing rule.

rules.hypothesis: After an extreme medium-horizon decline, a short-term momentum turn may mark the beginning of a reversal.
rules.mechanism: Investor overreaction can create later mean reversion.
rules.formalization_note: Very provisional crypto adaptation; original evidence is long-horizon equity data.

rules.hypothesis: After an extreme medium-horizon rise, a short-term momentum break may mark the beginning of a reversal.
rules.mechanism: Investor overreaction can create later mean reversion.

rules.hypothesis: Sentiment should be modelled explicitly and expected to matter most where valuation is subjective and arbitrage is constrained.
rules.mechanism: Sentiment interacts with limits to arbitrage.

rules.hypothesis: Consistent positive returns across short and medium horizons may reflect gradual belief updating and underreaction.
rules.mechanism: Belief biases can generate persistence after information arrives.

rules.hypothesis: Consistent negative returns across short and medium horizons may reflect gradual belief updating and underreaction.
rules.mechanism: Belief biases can generate persistence after information arrives.

rules.hypothesis: Gradual information diffusion can support continuation when price and activity confirm the same direction.
rules.mechanism: Short-run underreaction plus momentum trading.
rules.formalization_note: VERITAS proxy; does not directly measure information diffusion.

rules.hypothesis: Gradual information diffusion can support downside continuation when price and activity confirm the same direction.
rules.mechanism: Short-run underreaction plus momentum trading.

rules.hypothesis: When volatility and cross-venue dispersion rise together, arbitrage capacity may be impaired and apparent mispricing can widen rather than close.
rules.mechanism: Capital-constrained arbitrage can fail in extremes.
rules.formalization_note: Cross-venue divergence is a crypto proxy for stressed arbitrage conditions.

rules.hypothesis: Aggregate liquidity should be treated as a state variable and separate risk factor in asset allocation and signal validation.
rules.mechanism: Liquidity exposure is priced and varies through time.

rules.hypothesis: A strong aggressive-buy imbalance under elevated volume may contain information with persistent short-horizon price impact.
rules.mechanism: Informed trading moves prices through market depth.
rules.formalization_note: Taker-buy share and volume are proxies for signed order flow and market depth.

rules.hypothesis: A strong aggressive-sell imbalance under elevated volume may contain information with persistent short-horizon price impact.
rules.mechanism: Informed trading moves prices through market depth.

rules.hypothesis: Volatility forecasts should condition on recent volatility rather than assume constant variance.
rules.mechanism: Conditional heteroskedasticity and volatility clustering.

rules.hypothesis: An extreme current volatility state deserves reduced directional confidence because conditional volatility tends to persist.
rules.mechanism: Persistent conditional heteroskedasticity.
rules.formalization_note: Simple proxy pending a fitted GARCH/realized-volatility model.

rules.hypothesis: When VERITAS expands to equities, returns should be decomposed into systematic factor exposures before residual alpha is credited to a rule.
rules.mechanism: Multiple common factors explain expected returns.

rules.hypothesis: Equity-related signals should control for profitability and investment exposures as well as market, size and value factors.
rules.mechanism: Five-factor asset pricing structure.

rules.hypothesis: Benchmark factor datasets should be sourced from maintained canonical libraries and versioned to prevent silent methodology changes.
rules.mechanism: Reproducible empirical asset-pricing validation.

rules.hypothesis: Leverage constraints can distort risk pricing, so beta should not be assumed to map linearly into expected risk-adjusted return.
rules.mechanism: Constrained investors can overpay for high-beta exposure.

rules.hypothesis: When equities are added, quality characteristics should be tested jointly rather than treated as isolated heuristics.
rules.mechanism: Composite quality captures profitability, growth and safety dimensions.

rules.hypothesis: Independent styles should be evaluated jointly for diversification rather than promoting the strongest recent style in isolation.
rules.mechanism: Low correlation among style premia can improve portfolio robustness.

rules.hypothesis: Medium-horizon positive return with a positive trend is a simple crypto proxy for the broad momentum effect.
rules.mechanism: Momentum persistence across markets.
rules.formalization_note: Cross-asset adaptation, not a direct AQR trading rule.

rules.hypothesis: Medium-horizon negative return with a negative trend is a simple crypto proxy for the broad momentum effect.
rules.mechanism: Momentum persistence across markets.

rules.hypothesis: A positive trend confirmed over multiple horizons may proxy a time-series momentum state.
rules.mechanism: Managed-futures returns are substantially related to trend following.
rules.formalization_note: VERITAS trend proxy; requires transaction-cost-aware validation.

rules.hypothesis: A negative trend confirmed over multiple horizons may proxy a downside time-series momentum state.
rules.mechanism: Managed-futures returns are substantially related to trend following.

rules.hypothesis: Trend systems should be evaluated for skew and crisis behaviour, not only average returns, because their diversification value can be state dependent.
rules.mechanism: Trend following can exhibit positive skew and crisis-alpha properties.

rules.hypothesis: A simple positive trend filter may reduce exposure during persistent downtrends.
rules.mechanism: Trend-based tactical allocation.
rules.formalization_note: Crypto proxy; original framework uses longer moving-average horizons.

rules.hypothesis: A simple negative trend filter may identify persistent downside states.
rules.mechanism: Trend-based tactical allocation.
rules.formalization_note: Symmetric crypto adaptation; original framework is long/cash rather than short.

rules.hypothesis: Popular simple rules require bootstrap, parameter-stability and out-of-sample checks before being treated as persistent alpha.
rules.mechanism: Backtest success can be sample-dependent and overstated.

rules.hypothesis: Benchmark construction methodology can itself create systematic exposures and must be treated as an active modelling choice.
rules.mechanism: Cap weighting and fundamental weighting embed different economic tilts.

rules.hypothesis: High turnover or activity should not automatically be interpreted as information; overconfidence can itself create excessive trading.
rules.mechanism: Overconfidence can raise trading volume without proportionate information content.

rules.hypothesis: Positive price movement reinforced by activity can be consistent with short-run momentum generated by overconfidence and self-attribution.
rules.mechanism: Biased self-attribution can reinforce trends before longer-run correction.

rules.hypothesis: Negative price movement reinforced by activity can be consistent with short-run momentum generated by overconfidence and self-attribution.
rules.mechanism: Biased self-attribution can reinforce trends before longer-run correction.

rules.hypothesis: Liquidity stress should be modelled at the market level because execution deterioration can be correlated across instruments.
rules.mechanism: Liquidity has a common market-wide component.
rules.formalization_note: Governance until multi-venue liquidity data are added.

rules.hypothesis: Elevated funding, rapidly rising open interest and high volatility can proxy a leveraged state vulnerable to margin-driven dislocations.
rules.mechanism: Funding and margin constraints can amplify relative-value and liquidation stress.

rules.hypothesis: Leverage and balance-sheet expansion should be treated as procyclical state variables capable of amplifying risk-asset moves.
rules.mechanism: Intermediary leverage and liquidity are mutually reinforcing.
rules.formalization_note: Governance until broader leverage proxies are added.

rules.hypothesis: A price move must not be treated as informative solely because it is large; the causal layer must distinguish information from noise and liquidity effects.
rules.mechanism: Noise is intrinsic to market prices and trading.

rules.hypothesis: VERITAS should assume neither perfect efficiency nor free alpha; information advantages must be shown net of acquisition, execution and model costs.
rules.mechanism: Informational efficiency is limited when information is costly.

rules.hypothesis: A clearly defined positive move supported by activity may deserve trend-following participation.
rules.mechanism: Follow defined trends while cutting losses.
rules.formalization_note: Secondary-source proxy; exact Donchian channel breakout is not yet encoded.

rules.hypothesis: A clearly defined negative move supported by activity may deserve trend-following participation.
rules.mechanism: Follow defined trends while cutting losses.
rules.formalization_note: Secondary-source symmetric proxy; exact Donchian channels are not yet encoded.

rules.hypothesis: When market direction is not clearly defined, exposure should be light; losses should be limited and winners allowed room to persist.
rules.mechanism: Trend-following risk discipline.
